title: SIEVE: Overcoming Topological Obstruction in Equivariant Self-Supervised Learning
claim: Naive random masking destroys the geometric structure needed for reconstruction and collapses; our structure-preserving mask keeps it and reconstructs correctly.
layout: 2 stacked rows, left-to-right flow from shared input, dashed divider
description: Two horizontal rows share one input on the far left: a glossy torus point cloud labeled 'Point Cloud'. Large hollow arrows lead from it to the top row (Spherical Mask) and the bottom row (Random Mask), separated by a dashed line. Each row runs left to right through three stages: masked points, then 'Vector Encoding', then 'Equivariant Decoder'. In the top row, points on the torus are projected radially onto a translucent sphere, with a SphericalMask formula underneath. Light-blue dotted arcs then connect the encoded points back to a reconstructed torus, labeled 'Non-trivial Pullback V_Y' → Y' / Reconstruction'. In the bottom row, points scatter out of the torus into a rounded square, then become a structureless scatter. The scatter is labeled 'Trivial Pullback Y'×R^m → Y' / Topological Obstruction'. The eye goes first to the glossy sphere and torus at the top.
caption: Random masking causes representational collapse; spherical projection masking does not. Random masking functions ignore subtle geometric data inherent in point clouds. This imposes topological obstructions in reconstructing the desired non-trivial vector bundles characterizing the underlying geometry of point clouds, as demonstrated in Theorem [ref]. As a result, representational collapse can occur as shown in Section [ref]. SIEVE utilizes a spherical projection mask, thereby possessing capabilities in reconstructing a class of pullbacks of vector bundles defined over a wide variety of 2 and 3-dimensional manifolds as demonstrated in Theorem [ref].
abstract: We identify a theoretical incompatibility between 3D point cloud masked autoencoding and SE(3)-equivariant networks. We prove that standard masking triggers a topological collapse, effectively forcing the model to hallucinate orientation without a reference frame. To resolve this, we introduce SIEVE (Scalar Invariant Extraction Via Equivariance), an SE(3)-equivariant self-supervised framework that compresses point cloud geometry into invariant scalar embeddings. At its core is the spherical projection mask, which preserves global pose while obfuscating local semantics, sidestepping the obstruction by construction. Experiments confirm that SIEVE circumvents the predicted collapse where constant and noise masks fail. On downstream point cloud tasks, the resulting embeddings improve over coordinate-based baselines and hand-crafted geometric descriptors, with the largest gains on generalization to unseen shape categories.
